rotation_commentary.text: Par account (RBC Growth Insurance) seeded from shareholder surplus; long-term target 50% fixed income (govt 5%, corporate 30%, private FI 5%, rest short-term/mortgages) and 50% non-fixed income (common shares 50%, commercial real estate 0%, max 50%).
Public bond quality target AA 25% / A 50% / BBB 25%; sector target corporate 85% / provincial 15%; existing general-fund corporate book shown as reference.
Alternatives >C$2.5bn of >C$15bn (commercial mortgages, private fixed income, commercial real estate) - c.17% of team-managed assets.
LICAT total ratio fell 135% to 132% 'primarily attributable to new business growth', offset by retained earnings and capital transfer from other RBC Insurance legal entities.
Segment growth driven by longevity reinsurance and life retrocession (international); Q4 hit by annual actuarial assumption updates and reinsurance contract recaptures.

repos.text: OSFI LF3 'Asset Financing - Encumbered Assets - Repos' 3,625.4 = 14.1% of invested assets, far above peers (BMO Life, Co-operators Life report none). No public explanation found in RBC's annual/quarterly reports, AM Best releases or RBC Insurance materials. Plausible drivers (inferred, unverified): (i) collateral/liquidity management for a large derivative hedging book (FX notional 3,813; FI linear 2,782; FI non-linear 786) tied to longevity reinsurance/retrocession and seg-fund exposures; (ii) secured funding of spread assets using RBC Capital Markets as counterparty; (iii) capital transfers between RBC Insurance entities noted in the LICAT disclosure.

structured_indirect.text: Derivatives notional (OSFI LF3, Oct 31, 2025): currency 3,813.4; fixed income linear 2,781.7; fixed income non-linear 785.8; equity 179.4 - total c.7.6bn, 29.4% of portfolio.
Private assets >C$2.5bn: commercial mortgages, private fixed income, commercial real estate (team-managed). No CLO/ABS/fund-finance/sidecar exposure disclosed.

deals.text: RBC Insurance launches RBC Growth Insurance participating whole life (Oct 2023); par account seeded from shareholder surplus.
Growth in longevity reinsurance and life retrocession drives 14% segment earnings growth; Q4 recaptures of reinsurance contracts.
Insurance combined with Wealth Management under Neil McLaughlin as RBC integrates insurance, personal banking and wealth ('One RBC').

sponsorships.text: RBC Insurance community partners: Ronald McDonald House Charities, True Patriot Love, Junior Achievement, Park People, Wounded Warriors.

bank_relationships.text: Bank-owned: distribution through RBC branches/advice centres, proprietary sales force, third-party brokers and direct; investment team leverages RBC Capital Markets and RBC GAM.
Parent may provide capital at its discretion (no guarantee); capital transferred from other RBC Insurance legal entities in FY2025.

appetite: Not published for RBC Life; governed within RBC's enterprise risk appetite framework (RBC Annual Report risk section). AM Best assesses ERM as 'appropriate'.
governance: RBC Life board and OSFI supervision; group CRO Graeme Hepworth; RBC Insurance CRO not publicly named.
Par account: policyholder dividend scale set to smooth volatility; investment policy with target/min/max ranges.
risk.capital_target: Not disclosed. OSFI supervisory targets 100% total / 70% core; RBC Life at 132% / 109% (Oct 31, 2025).
sensitivities: None published by RBC Life; RBC group discloses insurance sensitivities only within consolidated market-risk disclosures (not entity-level).
hedging: Large derivative book vs portfolio (FX 14.8%, FI 13.9% of invested assets, OSFI LF3) consistent with FX and rate hedging of international reinsurance and seg-fund guarantees (inferred).
events: June 2026: Group Head Jennifer Publicover departs; Maria Winslow interim CEO; insurance folded under Wealth Management.
